subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should Telegram/ACP source turns enforce core tool-result-backed verification, only platform-owned delivery diagnostics/recovery, or documented non-verification when visible final text claims side effects?
rationale: The current code deliberately supports automatic final delivery and message-tool-only suppression, while a broader claim-verification request was already closed as plugin/ClawHub scope, so maintainers must choose the core boundary before implementation.

options.title: Define a narrow core invariant
options.body: Require core diagnostics or guarded recovery only for source-channel delivery gaps and side-effect claims that OpenClaw can verify from first-party tool/result evidence.

options.title: Keep broad verification plugin-owned
options.body: Leave arbitrary success-claim-to-ledger verification to plugins/ClawHub and document the current Telegram/ACP boundary.

options.title: Adopt broad core verification
options.body: Add a core claim ledger and enforcement policy, accepting the product and compatibility cost of blocking or warning on unsupported natural-language claims.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow core invariant
recommendation.body: Require core diagnostics or guarded recovery only for source-channel delivery gaps and side-effect claims that OpenClaw can verify from first-party tool/result evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest product-boundary signal from the related claim-verification closure and this issue needs a policy decision more than a local code owner decision.
